title: Skip to My Lou - A Skipping and Clapping Sing-Along for Toddlers
description: Skip, clap and stomp along with us to this happy old play-party song! #kidssong #nurseryrhyme #toddlersongs #singalong #dancesong
characters: Three adorable Black toddlers: Zuri, a 3-year-old girl with deep warm brown skin, round afro puffs tied with soft yellow fabric scrunchies, wearing a sunny yellow t-shirt, denim dungaree shorts and white sneakers; Kofi, a 4-year-old boy with medium-deep brown skin, short dark natural curly hair, wearing a blue t-shirt, grey jogger shorts and red sneakers; and Nala, a 3-year-old girl with deep brown skin, neat cornrow braids, wearing a yellow pinafore dress over a white t-shirt, white tights and pink sneakers

lines: Skip, skip, skip to my Lou
Skip, skip, skip to my Lou
Skip, skip, skip to my Lou
Skip to my Lou, my darling
verses.scene: The three toddlers skip in a happy line across a bright green lawn strung with colourful bunting.

lines: Clap your hands and skip to my Lou
Clap your hands and skip to my Lou
Stomp your feet and skip to my Lou
Skip to my Lou, my darling
verses.scene: The toddlers clap their hands high and stomp their feet in the grass, kicking up little leaves.

lines: Skip and clap along with me
Skip to my Lou, one, two, three
verses.scene: The three toddlers clap their hands together on the lawn, counting to three on their fingers.

lines: Round and round and skip to my Lou
Round and round and skip to my Lou
Wave hello and skip to my Lou
Skip to my Lou, my darling
verses.scene: The toddlers spin in a wide circle and wave both arms above their heads under a big blue sky.

lines: Skip and clap along with me
Skip to my Lou, one, two, three
verses.scene: The three toddlers clap their hands together on the lawn, counting to three on their fingers.

pd_source.author: Traditional (American play-party song)
pd_source.publication: An American play-party song documented from the 1840s and printed repeatedly in 19th-century American song collections.
pd_source.public_domain: Anonymous traditional text from the mid-19th century; expired copyright in the US (pre-1929) and worldwide.
pd_source.adaptation: The 'Skip, skip, skip to my Lou / Skip to my Lou, my darling' chorus is the traditional text verbatim. The traditional verses are an open-ended improvised set ('lost my partner, what'll I do'); verses 2 and 3 substitute toddler-friendly actions in exactly that tradition, and the hook is NEWLY WRITTEN.

song_style: children's nursery rhyme, cheerful upbeat kids song, cute female child voice, simple very repetitive catchy melody, lively skipping tempo, playful, bright, warm
